title: Gemini North’s Volatile Neighbor
caption: The Milky Way over Maunakea, with Mauna Loa in the distance, Hawaiʻi

recognition.text: NOIRLab Image of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The Milky Way's starry band hangs overhead in this panorama from Maunakea, home of Gemini North. On the mountain at the centre, a winding ribbon of light traces an access road. Far below, the large towns of the Island of Hawaiʻi glow in patches beneath the clouds, and the active volcano Mauna Loa rises above them.

Maunakea and Mauna Loa are both shield volcanoes, the broad, gently sloping kind built up by many flows of runny lava. The difference is that Maunakea is dormant, which is fortunate for the observatories on its summit.

The mountain's volcanic past still helps astronomers today. Its smooth, sloping sides and great height are two of the reasons the summit enjoys exceptional observing conditions. A high peak places telescopes above much of the atmosphere's moisture and turbulence.

understand.summary: This is a panoramic landscape photograph taken with a camera on Maunakea, in visible light. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long camera exposure gathers much more light than the eye, so the Milky Way looks brighter and more detailed than it would to someone on the summit.

alt: A panorama of the Milky Way above a dark mountain with a winding lit road, and a distant volcano rising above clouds lit by towns.
